title: Gap resolutions key on the raw project path while feature reads normalize it
body:
## Summary
gdd_gap_resolutions stores and matches project_path verbatim, while the audit's feature rows are scoped by normalizeProjectId, so two spellings of one project split its triage.

## Description
src/lib/gdd-compliance.ts resolvedGapIds / resolveGap / unresolveGap / listResolutions bind projectPath raw (`WHERE project_path = ?`); getFeaturesByModule (src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts) normalizes case, separators and trailing slash (src/lib/project-id.ts:23). Resolving under `C:\X\PoF\` and auditing under `c:/x/pof` re-opens every resolved gap; src/app/api/gdd-compliance/route.ts:26 forwards whatever spelling the client holds. Stored rows already hold raw spellings, so a fix must match both (normalize in JS on read like isInProjectScope, or a backfill) - why it is not Lane A here.

## Flow
- resolve a gap under 'C:\P\' -> row project_path='C:\P\'
- audit under 'c:/p' -> resolvedGapIds('c:/p') finds 0 -> gap shows open
- fix: compare normalizeProjectId on both sides, or backfill + normalize on write

## Expected impact
Triage survives a project-path spelling change; touches stored rows, one in-tree route caller.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one identity rule for the audit's two inputs
Before: project-identity normalization on the audit's 2 reads: 1 of 2
After: 2 of 2; a resolved gap stays resolved across spellings
Method: simulation - walked the 4 SQL sites; stored raw spellings need a read-side match or backfill decision, not built
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route test: resolve under 'C:\P\', audit under 'c:/p' expects resolved:true (red before)

title: Review history and latest delta mix own and legacy snapshot series
body:
## Summary
getReviewHistory, getAllReviewHistory and getLatestReviewDelta read review_snapshots own-OR-legacy, so a named project's sparkline interleaves its points with the legacy bucket's and the latest delta can diff a legacy point against an owned one.

## Description
src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts getReviewHistory / getAllReviewHistory / getLatestReviewDelta use projectScopeSql (own + ''), while feature-row reads moved to shadowedScopeSql to stop double-listing. Snapshots have no per-feature key to shadow, so pre-attribution legacy history and post-attribution own history plot as one line, and getLatestReviewDelta pairs rows[0]/rows[1] across the two series. Which history a project should see after attribution (own only, or both labelled) is a product call.

## Flow
- insert a legacy snapshot @T1 (10 implemented) and an own snapshot @T2 (2 implemented)
- the sparkline reads 10 -> 2: a regression that never happened
- the delta diffs legacy feature_states against own

## Expected impact
Trend lines and 'what moved' stop reporting cross-series jumps; could hide legacy history the operator wants.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one series per trend line
Before: series merged into one sparkline for a project holding both legacy and own snapshots: 2
After: 1 (or 2, labelled)
Method: simulation - read the three queries; the view rule is a product decision
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence: src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts getReviewHistory (WHERE module_id = ? AND ${scope.sql}), getLatestReviewDelta (LIMIT 2 over own+legacy)
instrument: operator picks own-only vs labelled dual series; then a db test with one legacy + one own snapshot

title: Prompt section audits omit sections build() renders
body:
## Summary
PromptBuilder.audit() has no row for the quality pack build() renders; auditPromptString misses assetSpec and qualityPack, and its successCriteria cue matches any numbered list.

## Description
src/lib/prompts/prompt-builder.ts build() pushes _qualityPack and _assetSpec; audit() lists 8 sections without qualityPack, and auditPromptString (read by src/components/modules/shared/PromptInspector.tsx:66) lists 7 without either. Its successCriteria regex `^\d+\.\s` (multiline) is satisfied by any numbered Instructions list, so the chip reads present on prompts with no Success Criteria section. Three hand-maintained lists of one section set, none derived from the others. Fixed = one SECTION_ORDER constant feeding build(), audit() and the string audit, with a criteria cue tied to the heading.

## Flow
- build with withQualityPack + withAssetSpec -> audit() reports neither
- auditPromptString on a prompt with '## Instructions\n1. ...' and no criteria -> successCriteria present
- derive the lists from one constant; test list equality

## Expected impact
The Prompt Inspector chip strip tells the truth about coverage; chip counts change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - audit lists derived from the render order
Before: section lists in sync with build(): 0 of 2; false-present successCriteria on numbered instructions: yes
After: 2 of 2; no
Method: simulation - read build() vs both audit lists; the PromptInspector test needs re-pinning (outside paths)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/prompts/prompt-builder.ts audit() (no qualityPack row), auditPromptString (7 rows; /^\d+\.\s/m)
src/components/modules/shared/PromptInspector.tsx:66
instrument: test: the audit lists equal the sections build() can emit; numbered-instructions prompt without criteria -> successCriteria false

title: diffPrompts allocates a full n*m LCS table with no prefix/suffix trim
body:
## Summary
text-diff's lcsOps builds an (n+1)x(m+1) matrix over the whole prompt even when one line changed, and CRLF input diffs every line.

## Description
src/lib/text-diff.ts lcsOps allocates `Array.from({ length: n + 1 }, () => new Array(m + 1))`; a 2000-line before/after with one edit is ~4.0M cells and O(n*m) time, where trimming the shared prefix/suffix first reduces the table to the changed hunk. splitLines splits on '\n' only, so CRLF vs LF of the same text marks every line changed.

## Flow
- time diffPrompts on 500/2000-line prompts with one changed line
- add prefix/suffix trim (and a trailing '\r' strip) before lcsOps
- re-time; diff rows must be identical

## Expected impact
The Prompt Optimizer diff stays fast on long prompts; risk: row pairing changes if the trim is wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - diff cost proportional to the changed region
Before: cells for a 2000-line one-edit diff: ~4.0M; time unmeasured
After: a handful of cells; time unmeasured
Method: simulation - counted from the allocation formula; no timing taken
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/text-diff.ts lcsOps (dp = Array.from({ length: n + 1 }, ...))
src/lib/text-diff.ts splitLines (s.split('\n'))
instrument: microbench: diffPrompts on 2000-line inputs with one edit, before/after trim, plus an output-equality test

title: hashChecklist is copy-pasted between the compliance store and the GDD hook
body:
## Summary
The checklist staleness hash is defined twice, in src/stores/gddComplianceStore.ts and src/hooks/useGameDesignDoc.ts.

## Description
src/hooks/useGameDesignDoc.ts hashChecklist is a verbatim copy of src/stores/gddComplianceStore.ts hashChecklist; its comment says it is 're-implemented here because that one is store-private'. Two copies of one freshness key drift independently. Fixed = one exported pure helper (e.g. in src/lib/checklist-progress.ts) both import.

## Flow
- grep 'function hashChecklist' -> 2 definitions
- extract to a lib and import in both
- the staleness-gate tests stay green

## Expected impact
No user-visible change; removes a drift risk.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of the checklist freshness key
Before: definitions: 2
After: 1
Method: probe - grep counted both copies; extraction lands in a lib outside these paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: grep count of 'function hashChecklist' == 1 + both staleness test files green

title: POST /api/feature-matrix leaves optional row fields untyped, so a wrong type is a 500
body:
## Summary
qualityScore, nextSteps and lastReviewedAt are not type-checked on POST; an object for nextSteps or lastReviewedAt reaches the better-sqlite3 bind and fails as a 500.

## Description
src/app/api/feature-matrix/route.ts validates the required fields (and, tonight, status and filePaths elements). upsertFeatures binds `f.nextSteps ?? ''` and `normalizeReviewTimestamp(f.lastReviewedAt)`, which returns a non-string unchanged when Date.parse is NaN - an object binds and throws 'SQLite3 can only bind numbers, strings, bigints, buffers, and null' -> withRoute 500. The import route rejects these via zod. Fixed = a 400 naming a present-but-wrong-typed optional field.

## Flow
- POST features:[{...complete, nextSteps:{}}]
- -> 500 bind error
- fix: 400 naming the field

## Expected impact
Malformed callers get an actionable 400; no in-tree caller sends these wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a caller error is a 400, not a 500
Before: optional-field type checks on POST: 0 of 3
After: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - traced the bind path; not probed this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/app/api/feature-matrix/route.ts POST row check (no qualityScore/nextSteps/lastReviewedAt)
src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts upsertFeatures stmt.run(... f.nextSteps ?? '', ..., normalizeReviewTimestamp(f.lastReviewedAt))

title: restoreVariant matches the held history by checklist item only, not module
body:
## Summary
restoreVariant flips loaded variants by (moduleId, checklistItemId) but updates versionHistory when only checklistItemId matches.

## Description
src/stores/promptEvolutionStore.ts restoreVariant: the variants map checks `v.moduleId === restored.moduleId && v.checklistItemId === restored.checklistItemId`; the history guard is `s.versionHistory.checklistItemId !== restored.checklistItemId` only. Checklist item ids are per-module, so a restore in module B with an item id shared by the held module-A history flips A's active flags. Fixed = guard on both keys.

## Flow
- hold history for (module A, item x)
- restore a variant of (module B, item x)
- A's history marks B's variant active

## Expected impact
The History tab cannot show a foreign module's active version; depends on cross-module id overlap.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one key rule for the two local mirrors
Before: guard keys: variants 2, history 1
After: 2 and 2
Method: simulation - read both guards; cross-module id overlap not counted this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: store test: history held for (A,x), restore (B,x) -> history unchanged

title: loadTests and clusterPrompts are unsequenced per-module loaders
body:
## Summary
loadTests(moduleId) and clusterPrompts(moduleId) commit whichever response arrives last, unlike the three sequenced loaders.

## Description
src/stores/promptEvolutionStore.ts loadTests and clusterPrompts `set({ abTests })` / `set({ clusters })` with no request token; switching modules fast can leave the previous module's tests or clusters on screen. loadVariants, loadSuggestions and (tonight) loadVersionHistory follow latest-wins.

## Flow
- select module A, then B, with A's get-tests slower
- abTests shows A's tests under B

## Expected impact
The Tests and Clusters tabs match the selected module; low risk.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - latest-wins on every per-module loader
Before: sequenced per-module loaders: 3 of 5
After: 5 of 5
Method: simulation - walked both loaders; the instrument is the history-race test built tonight
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/stores/promptEvolutionStore.ts loadTests (set({ abTests })), clusterPrompts (set({ clusters, isClustering: false }))
instrument: per-loader race test (deferred fetch, B resolves before A) expecting B

title: Interactive Mermaid nodes get tabindex but no visible focus style
body:
## Summary
MermaidDiagram makes nodes role=button with tabindex=0 but applies no focus indicator; SVG <g> elements draw no default outline in most browsers.

## Description
src/components/ui/MermaidDiagram.tsx sets cursor, role, tabindex and aria-label on each .node but no focus class or :focus-visible style, while the repo ships a focus-ring token (--focus-accent). Keyboard users tabbing the GDD architecture diagram cannot see which module node is focused (WCAG 2.4.7).

## Flow
- Tab into the architecture diagram
- focus moves through nodes with no visible indicator
- fix: an SVG focus-visible stroke from the focus-accent token

## Expected impact
Keyboard focus becomes visible on diagram nodes; could clash with mermaid's node styles.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - visible keyboard focus on interactive nodes
Before: interactive nodes with a focus style: 0
After: all
Method: simulation - read the effect; jsdom cannot render focus, needs a browser check
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/ui/MermaidDiagram.tsx node.setAttribute('tabindex', '0') with no focus style
instrument: browser screenshot of a focused node (or a style-presence test on the rendered SVG)
